query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A modified nozzle configuration for the HVAF-i7 torch—specifically, a convergent nozzle extension that effectively reduces the spray distance (targeting an effective distance of 300–350 mm) to boost particle velocity—will increase the built‐up thickness of FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coats while maintaining their as-sprayed microstructural quality (low oxidation and sound adhesion).
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder with a 15–45 μm size distribution, which when sprayed with the standard HVAF-i7 configuration produces acceptable quality coatings but with insufficient thickness.
generation.intervention: Retrofitting the HVAF-i7 torch with a convergent nozzle extension that reduces the effective spray distance to around 300–350 mm, thereby increasing the in-flight particle velocity without altering the feedstock composition.
generation.conditions: Deposition performed in the HVAF-i7 process on substrates (including internal diameters as small as 120 mm) under conditions typical for bond-coat applications; service conditions include high-temperature thermal-barrier environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced particle kinetic energy that improves in-flight splat formation and inter-splat consolidation, leading to a thicker, denser coating while preserving the limited oxidation built into the as-sprayed microstructure.
generation.mechanism: The nozzle extension will concentrate and accelerate the spray plume, increasing the impact energy of powder particles. This boost in kinetic energy promotes improved deformation and bonding upon substrate impact, resulting in a higher deposition efficiency and thicker coating buildup. At the same time, by maintaining an optimized spraying distance, the thermal exposure is controlled to limit in-spray oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline (15–45 μm feedstock with the standard HVAF-i7 setup), the modified nozzle should result in a significantly thicker, well‐adhered bond coat that retains its microstructural integrity and minimal oxidation—meeting the design target for high-temperature service, even within constrained geometries.
generation.baseline: Current HVAF-i7 depositions using 15–45 μm feedstock (without the nozzle extension) achieve acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
generation.boundary: The improved deposition should hold under typical HVAF-i7 operating conditions and for spray applications in geometries with internal diameters as small as 120 mm; the intervention’s benefit must not come at the expense of significantly increased as-sprayed oxidation or deterioration of coating adhesion.
generation.uncertainty: This proposal extrapolates from evidence in the MCrAlY bond coat studies (which showed improved deposition efficiency at spray distances of 300–350 mm) and from the success of the HVAF-M3 system using similar feedstock sizes, but it remains uncertain how the unique plume dynamics and thermal profiles of the HVAF-i7 system will respond to a nozzle modification. Moreover, the impact on in-flight oxidation under the accelerated conditions is yet to be fully characterized.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a controlled deposition experiment on identical substrates (including samples with narrow internal diameters of 120 mm) using the HVAF-i7 torch in two configurations: (i) the standard nozzle setup and (ii) the modified nozzle with a convergent extension. Maintain all other process parameters (e.g., powder feed rate, gas composition, and torch traverse speed) constant.
measurements: Microstructural integrity (via SEM and EDS to evaluate oxidation levels and splat morphology)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nozzle-modified HVAF-i7 deposition does not yield a statistically significant increase in coating thickness (with maintained low oxidation and adhesion properties comparable to or better than the baseline) or if it leads to unacceptable increases in oxidation or degradation in coating integrity, then the hypothesis is falsified.
